findings.description: Missing epistemic flags section. The post makes falsifiable empirical claims (52% crystallization rate, zero false negatives target) and applies psychometric theory to software architecture, yet carries no formal epistemic flags block. The project convention mandates epistemic flags in all substantive analytical output.
findings.suggestion: Add a standard epistemic flags section before the closing paragraph. Flag at minimum: (1) the 52% figure derives from a single 123-message production run, not a validated sample; (2) the triage scoring thresholds represent engineering judgment without empirical calibration data; (3) the Cattell analogy carries transfer risk from psychometrics to software architecture.
findings.context: Post ends with attribution line — no epistemic flags block precedes it.

findings.description: Missing epistemic flags section. The post presents a structured decision methodology with claims about calibration, anchoring bias mitigation, and decision quality improvement. No epistemic flags section appears. The convention applies to all substantive analytical output.
findings.suggestion: Add an epistemic flags section. Flag at minimum: (1) the two-pass calibration claim (reduces anchoring bias) describes design intention, not measured effect; (2) the single case study (auth sequencing) cannot demonstrate generalizability; (3) LLM non-determinism limits reproducibility claims.

findings.convergence_note: Braver Angels attribution pattern flagged in scan-008, scan-009, and now scan-010. Fixed in action/index.astro but persists in sibling content files.
findings.description: Braver Angels described as 'the nation's largest cross-partisan citizen movement' without attribution. This presents a self-reported superlative as editorial fact. The action/index.astro page already models the correct hedged phrasing ('which describes itself as').
findings.suggestion: Change to: 'Braver Angels, which describes itself as the nation's largest cross-partisan citizen movement' — matching the hedging already applied in action/index.astro.
findings.context: Braver Angels, the nation's largest cross-partisan citizen movement, demonstrates that structured dialogue across political differences produces agreement more effectively than persuasion.

findings.description: Same Braver Angels attribution gap. 'the nation's largest cross-partisan citizen movement' appears without hedging, presenting a self-reported superlative as established fact.
findings.suggestion: Add attribution hedge: 'which describes itself as' — consistent with the pattern already established in action/index.astro.
findings.context: Braver Angels, the nation's largest cross-partisan citizen movement, demonstrates that structured dialogue across political differences produces common ground more effectively than persuasion.

findings.description: Multiple E-prime violations in body text. Approximately 10 instances of 'is/are' forms where active verbs could replace them. Examples: 'The boundary between crystallized and fluid processing is not fixed' (line 203), 'The triage scoring is our current best model' (line 234).
findings.suggestion: Rewrite 'The boundary... is not fixed' to 'The boundary... shifts as experience accumulates' (the next sentence already does this). Rewrite 'The triage scoring is our current best model' to 'The triage scoring represents our current best model.'
findings.context: The boundary between crystallized and fluid processing is not fixed. It shifts as experience accumulates.

findings.description: The claim 'The same decision with the same inputs produces the same analysis' overstates reproducibility. LLM outputs exhibit non-deterministic variation even with identical prompts. This presents design intention (the architecture aims for reproducibility) as observation (it produces identical results).
findings.suggestion: Rewrite to acknowledge the aspiration/observation distinction: 'The same decision with the same inputs produces structurally comparable analysis' or 'The architecture aims to make reasoning auditable and repeatable across runs.'
findings.context: The cognitive architecture doesn't make the agent smarter. It makes the agent's reasoning auditable, repeatable, and calibrated. The same decision with the same inputs produces the same analysis...

findings.description: The claim that the UDHR drafting committee 'likely included people who had encountered this correspondence' and that 'it had circulated among diplomats and intellectuals' reads as established fact without a citation. The epistemic flags section acknowledges the indirect evidence, but the body text does not cite a source for the circulation claim.
findings.suggestion: Add a citation (e.g., Morsink's UDHR historiography) or strengthen the hedging: 'may have included people who had encountered this correspondence — evidence suggests it had circulated among diplomats.'
findings.context: The UDHR drafting committee likely included people who had encountered this correspondence — it had circulated among diplomats and intellectuals involved in postwar institution-building.

findings.description: Heading hierarchy inconsistency. The post begins with an H1 duplicating the frontmatter title. Five of the other seven posts scanned use H2 as the top-level body heading, relying on the rendering engine to generate H1 from frontmatter.
findings.suggestion: Remove the H1 at line 31 or convert to H2, matching the convention used by other posts in the blog.
findings.context: # Pattern Generators for AI Minds (line 31) followed by ## Your Brain Runs on Autopilot (line 33)
